slides.say: A pyramid has a square base with side four root two. Each slanted edge is seven. What is the height of the pyramid?
at: A pyramid has a square base
A pyramid has a square base

slides.say: We'll solve it in two different ways, the math way, and then with an estimate. Let's start with the math way.
We want the height, so let's call it h. Honestly, at first it's not clear where to start. The height just hangs there in the middle. What's given? The slanted edge, seven.
So, like in the lesson, we build a triangle inside the pyramid. We join the foot of the height, O, to the corner B. Now P O B is a triangle.
at: Now P O B is a triangle

slides.say: It's a right triangle. Why? The height stands straight on the base, so it makes a right angle with every line on the base from its foot. O B is such a line.
The hypotenuse is the edge, seven. We need the other leg, O B. The foot of the height is the middle of the square, where the diagonals meet. So O B is half of a diagonal.
Remember the silver triangle. The diagonal of a square is the side times root two. Four root two times root two is four times two, eight. Half of it is four. So O B is four.
at: Four root two times root two

slides.say: Let's pull the triangle out. A leg of four and a hypotenuse of seven. That's not a triple we know, so we use Pythagoras. h squared plus four squared is seven squared.
So h squared is forty-nine minus sixteen, thirty-three. Thirty-three has no whole root, so h is root thirty-three. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Now let's estimate. The slanted edge is seven. Must the height be less than seven?
Yes. The height is the shortest way from the top point down to the base. The edge is slanted, so it's longer. So the height is less than seven.
Our anchor is root forty-nine, which is exactly seven. So the height is less than root forty-nine.
Choice number one, seven root two. Root two is more than one, so this is more than seven. Out.
Choice number two, root thirty-three. It's less than root forty-nine. So it's possible. Not certain yet, but possible, so we keep it.
Choice number three, root sixty-five. It's more than root forty-nine, more than seven. Out.
Choice number four, five root two. Let's put the five under the root. Five squared is twenty-five, times two is fifty. Root fifty is just above root forty-nine, so it's out.
Three choices are out, so it's the fourth one left. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
